title: The Alphabetically Smallest Rotation of a Word

concept.title: Compare two candidate starts letter by letter; the loser, and the next k starts after it, can never be the minimum
body: A rotation of a word moves some letters from the front to the back. The rotations of `cabab` are `cabab, ababc, babca, abcab, bcaba`; the alphabetically smallest is `ababc`. Generating and comparing all `n` rotations costs O(n^2).

Keep two candidate starting positions `i` and `j` (at the start `0` and `1`) and a length `k` of the part where the two rotations have been found equal. Compare the letters `s[(i + k) mod n]` and `s[(j + k) mod n]`. If they are equal, increase `k`. If the letter at `i` is **larger**, then the rotations starting at `i, i + 1, ..., i + k` can never be the smallest: each of them is beaten by the rotation that starts the same number of letters later at `j` (it has the same first `k` letters of the comparison and a smaller next letter, or reaches a smaller one), so we can skip them all: `i += k + 1`. If the letter at `j` is larger, do `j += k + 1`. Restart `k = 0` and make sure `i != j`. When one of the pointers reaches `n` or `k = n`, the smaller of `i` and `j` is the start of the smallest rotation.

body.code:
i, j, k = 0, 1, 0
while i < n and j < n and k < n:
    a, b = s[(i + k) % n], s[(j + k) % n]
    if a == b:
        k += 1; continue
    if a > b: i += k + 1      # the starts i .. i + k lose to the starts j .. j + k
    else:     j += k + 1
    if i == j: j += 1
    k = 0
start = min(i, j)
print(s[start:] + s[:start])

body: Every step of the loop moves `i`, `j` or `k` forward in a way that the total number of steps is at most `3n`, so the algorithm is O(n). If the word is periodic, several starts give the same rotation, and the printed word is the same whichever is found. This is the *minimal cyclic shift* (Booth or two-pointer algorithm).

statement: A word `s` is given. Print the alphabetically smallest of its rotations (a rotation moves some letters from the beginning to the end).
constraints: The word consists of lowercase English letters.
hints: Keep two candidate starts i and j and the length k of the common part.
If the letter at i is larger, skip the starts i .. i + k; if the letter at j is larger, skip j .. j + k.
The smaller pointer at the end is the start of the answer.

explanation: Two candidate starts are compared letter by letter; the start with the larger letter and the k starts after it are discarded, and the smaller pointer at the end gives the smallest rotation.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

s = input().strip()

n = len(s)
i, j, k = 0, 1, 0
while i < n and j < n and k < n:
    a = s[(i + k) % n]
    b = s[(j + k) % n]
    if a == b:
        k += 1
        continue
    if a > b:
        i += k + 1
    else:
        j += k + 1
    if i == j:
        j += 1
    k = 0
start = min(i, j)
print(s[start:] + s[:start])
